correctness.rationale: The exact Ehrenfest transition-row generating polynomial is A(z)^i B(z)^(n−i) with p=(1−a)/2,q=(1+a)/2; summing rows gives [B(z)^(n+1)−A(z)^(n+1)]/[a(1−z)]. The binomial likelihood ratio switches only once, so unique central column maximizes unweighted ℓ1. Differentiating the central binomial tail gives c_n/a integral_0^a(1−s²)^m ds, increasing from1 to c_n. Quotient Boolean-cube row absolute-derivative sums imply exact infinity norm 2 n a P(Bin(n−1,p)=floor np); local binomial CLT, uniform small/large time bound imply (γ+o(1))sqrt n. At a=n^(−1/2), t=(log n)/4, central-column derivative C_m′(t)/sqrt n->4β, hence M1>=(β+o(1))sqrt n log n. Individually checked 15 finite Q-matrix examples; no matching upper asymptotic of M1 is claimed.
